summary.description: Heptachlor is a chlorinated pesticide, appearing as a white or tan powder with a camphor-like odor. It is highly stable and persistent in the environment.
environmental_impact: Heptachlor accumulates in soil, sediment, and body fat of animals and humans due to its lipophilic nature.
It persists in the environment for decades because of its chemical stability.
Toxic effects in animals include liver damage, increased excitability, infertility, and it is classified as a possible human carcinogen.

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Heptachlor is toxic and a possible human carcinogen, causing serious health risks including liver damage and reproductive harm.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Its persistence and bioaccumulation highlight the need for responsible pesticide use and waste management to reduce environmental contamination.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: Heptachlor contaminates soil and accumulates in terrestrial animals, causing toxic effects and threatening biodiversity.
